Proposal

Local devices through a Python sidecar

proposal/device-sidecar2026-11-20Giovanni Porcaridraft

Problem

A GenroPy page in a browser cannot reach the devices of the machine it runs on. The downloadable app exists to give the page that access, and the card reader is only the first device. The next ones are:

  • local printers and label printers;
  • medical devices, for example ultrasound scanners;
  • industry 4.0 equipment: PLCs, sensors, machines;
  • other serial, USB or network devices.

The device code must be written in Python, the language of the GenroPy team and of the existing signing agent of icond. Writing each device in Rust inside the Tauri shell does not scale.

The cases are hundreds: every customer has its own machines, scales, readers and label printers. A module for a new device must reach the computers of that customer without a new release of GenroApp, and only those computers.

Current state

  • GenroApp (this repository): Tauri 2 shell with the card logic in Rust, src-tauri/src/card.rs. See the booklet.
  • icond signing agent (firmatore_mac/, branch firma-digitale-protocolli): Python app in the menu bar or tray, PyKCS11, polls icond every 30 seconds. On Windows it is a 32-bit PyInstaller build, because the bit4id DLL of Firma4NG is 32-bit only.
  • Mobile: Android and iOS apps are built with Capacitor.

Proposed solution

The app is split in two processes. A thin shell shows the GenroPy page and guards the access. A Python process, the sidecar, owns every device. The shell never changes when a device is added.

Shell

  • Window without browser chrome, instance URL, menu: as in the current runner.
  • One generic command for the page: device_call(module, method, params). The shell forwards it to the sidecar and returns the answer.
  • Device events (an image received, a PLC value changed) arrive from the sidecar and the shell emits them to the page, which receives them with listen.
  • Permission per origin, as today: only the origin of the configured URL gets device_call. In addition config.json lists the modules that origin may use.
  • Local windows for what the page must not see or decide alone: card PIN, confirmation of an action. The sidecar asks the shell to open them.
  • Tray icon: the app keeps running with the window closed, for the devices that send data by themselves.
  • Starts the sidecar at launch, restarts it if it exits, stops it on quit.

Sidecar protocol

One JSON object per line. The shell writes requests on the sidecar stdin and reads answers and events on its stdout. The sidecar writes its log on stderr.

  • A request carries id; its answer carries the same id with result or error.
  • An event carries event and no id.
  • A ui line is a request from the sidecar to the shell: open a local window and answer with the same id.
  • At startup the sidecar sends one line with its modules and their methods. The sidecar itself refuses an unknown module or method with the error code unknown.

Modules

One Python module per device class, in sidecar/modules/. A module exposes its methods with a decorator; the registry builds the startup list from them.

Implemented: system and inbox, described in the booklet. Next modules, in this order:

  1. printers: direct print of a PDF with lp (CUPS, AirPrint printers included) and the macOS print panel through PDFKit. On Windows pywin32.
  2. photos: the system picker, where the user chooses the photos and the app receives only those. Full library access through PhotoKit needs NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription in the Info.plist of the bundle.
  3. cards: tessere.py of icond with its logic unchanged. The Rust card.rs is removed once cards works.

Modules installed on the client

A module for one customer is not frozen in the app. It is a package downloaded on the computers of that customer and loaded by the sidecar at start.

  1. Softwell builds the package of a module: its Python sources, the pure Python libraries it needs, and a manifest with name, version and the origins of the sites that may call it.
  2. Softwell signs the manifest with the Ed25519 key that signs the RunDoc. The manifest carries the SHA-256 of every file of the package.
  3. A saved site offers its modules at a fixed address, like /_tools/rundoc. GenroApp downloads them, verifies the signature and the hashes, and checks that the origin of the site is in the manifest.
  4. GenroApp writes the package to app_config_dir/modules/<name>/<version>/ and restarts the sidecar.
  5. The sidecar adds that folder to sys.path and imports the modules after its own. The registry and device_call do not change.
  6. The shell grants device_call for a module only to the origins of its manifest.
must
GenroApp loads only modules whose manifest carries a valid Softwell signature and whose files match the hashes of the manifest.
a module is code that runs on the computer of the user: an unsigned one lets a compromised site run any code there
must
A module is callable only from the origins listed in its signed manifest.
On macOS a module with native libraries (.so, .dylib) loads only if those libraries are signed with the Softwell Developer ID: the hardened runtime refuses unsigned libraries, and the app keeps that check. Pure Python modules have no such limit.
Third-party libraries of a module travel in its package. The frozen sidecar holds only the standard library and the libraries of the built-in modules.

The window Gestione of GenroApp lists the installed modules with version and origins, and removes one.

Built-in devices and downloaded modules

Two places for device code:

  • Built into GenroApp, in Rust: the few devices every customer has, always the same. Signature cards (card.rs, PKCS#11), local and label printers (lp, raw ZPL on port 9100), fiscal cash registers. They work in the distributed build, without the sidecar.
  • Downloaded Python modules: everything specific to one customer. Machines at the operator station (OPC UA, Modbus, Siemens S7), scales, serial and USB readers, medical devices.

Machines read continuously, with no operator, do not belong in GenroApp: they need a process on the server side of the plant that runs with no app open.

Packaging

  • The sidecar is frozen with PyInstaller and shipped inside the app bundle, next to the shell.
  • On Windows the sidecar is a 32-bit build, as the icond agent is today, so it loads the bit4id DLL. The shell stays 64-bit: it never loads the DLL.
  • macOS: shell and sidecar are signed with the same Developer ID and notarized together.

Why Tauri for the shell

With the Python sidecar the shell is a small fixed layer: window, permissions, forwarding, local windows, tray, updates. The choice is between shells that can host it.

Shell options

Window without browser chromeYesYesYesNo

Windows 32-bitTarget i686-pc-windows-msvcLast ia32 build: 43.0.0; none from 44.0.0Depends on the Python buildAgent only
Language of the shellRustJavaScript (Node)PythonPython
  • Electron is the more mature option. It has had releases since 2016, the same Chromium on every system, and its shell would be JavaScript, a language the team already writes.
  • Tauri is proposed for three reasons. Access control per origin is built in and already tested in the runner; in Electron it is hand-written code in every handler, and an error there exposes the devices to any page. The bundle is several times smaller. The shell already exists and works.
  • The macOS engine is already in use. Tauri on macOS runs WebKit, the engine of Safari and of the iOS apps, where the GenroPy client is used every day.
  • The 32-bit limit of Electron does not decide. With the sidecar the shell never loads the bit4id DLL.
  • The choice can be reversed. The sidecar and its protocol do not depend on the shell. Moving to Electron rewrites only the shell layer: forwarding, origin checks, local windows, tray.
  • pywebview would give one language, but no access control and no updater: both would have to be written. Agent + browser keeps the browser address bar and needs a local HTTP port reachable from the page. Capacitor for Electron (@capacitor-community/electron) is stopped at 5.0.1 of September 2023, for Capacitor 5, while Capacitor is at 8.6.0.

Decisions

proposedd-shell
Which shell hosts the GenroPy page and the sidecar?
  1. Tauri 2

    Built-in per-origin access, small bundle, existing runner.

  2. Electron

    More mature, Chromium everywhere, shell in JavaScript. Access control written by hand.

proposedd-protocol
How do shell and sidecar talk?
  1. JSON lines on stdin/stdout

    No port opened, the sidecar lives and dies with the app.

  2. Local HTTP or WebSocket

    Easier to debug with curl, but a port on the machine that other processes can reach.

proposedd-modules
Which modules may the page use?
  1. List per origin in config.json

    The shell refuses a call to a module the origin is not granted.

  2. All modules for the configured origin
decidedd-data-path
How does data from a device reach the GenroPy server?
  1. Through the page

    The sidecar emits an event, the page sends the data with an RPC. Works only with the page open.

  2. Sidecar to server

    The sidecar posts to the server with a token, as the icond agent does. Works with the window closed.

Choice: Through the page (GP, 2026-11-04)
The page uploads with the session of the logged-in user. Data that arrives with the app closed waits for the next opening.
proposedd-builtin
Where do signature cards, printers and cash registers live?
  1. Built into GenroApp, in Rust

    They work in the distributed build with no Python runtime. A change needs a new release of GenroApp.

  2. Sidecar modules

    One mechanism for every device. The distributed build always carries the Python runtime.

proposedd-module-source
How does a module reach the computer of a customer?
  1. Frozen in the sidecar

    Every module is in every app. A new module needs a new release.

  2. Downloaded signed package

    A module reaches only the sites listed in its manifest, without a new release. Needs the signature and hash checks above.

opend-medical
Does processing images and reports from medical devices make the app medical device software under the MDR? Images and reports are health data under the GDPR in any case. To clarify before distributing the medical modules.
  1. Not medical device software: data transfer only
  2. Medical device software: certification needed

Consequences

  • The repository gains a sidecar/ Python package with its own tests and PyInstaller spec.
  • With built-in devices in Rust, src-tauri/src/card.rs stays and the cards module of the sidecar is not written.
  • Softwell gains a second signing duty: module packages, with the key of the RunDoc.
  • Builds become two per platform (shell and sidecar), joined in one bundle and one installer.
  • Modules with listeners (DICOM Storage, HL7, MQTT) open ports on the local network. The icond agent never does; each such port is a configuration choice per installation.
  • Mobile stays on Capacitor. A page can detect the platform with window.Capacitor, window.__TAURI__ or neither.
